title: Add benchmark-lab inference-scaling and profiling reporting pipeline
author: Ethan Park
description:
Motivation: we need an end-to-end reporting pipeline that (1) runs representative workload runners across scale points (1/4, 1/2, full capacity) for common inference shapes, (2) captures kernel-level profiling baselines and kernel-selection traces, and (3) stores aggregated metrics for the benchmark lab dashboard and automated regression detection. This PR wires together workload runners, a profiling collector, and the reporting ETL to publish perf baselines and scaling curves.

Scope: add new CI job definitions, a small agent that orchestrates runners and profiling capture, ETL job to ingest perf artifacts into telemetry storage, dashboard metadata, and a handful of canonical workload configs (chat-short, chat-long, embedding-batch).

Checklist:
- [x] Add workload runner configs and workload runner orchestration agent
- [x] Add profiling collector (nvprof/roctracer wrappers + lightweight kernel selection tracing)
- [x] Add ETL job + schema mapping to benchmark metrics tables
- [x] Add CI pipeline for nightly runs and canary on merge
- [x] Add dashboard metadata and perf-suite definitions to benchmark-lab catalog
- [x] Add tests: unit for ETL transforms, integration smoke test that runs one config in CI container

Testing/Validation: unit tests for ETL and config parsing added under benchmark-lab/test; integration job added to CI (nightly-ml-bench). Local run validated on single-GPU dev box and on dedicated benchmark lab pool (full-run captured scaling curves). Generated baseline artifacts uploaded to internal S3 path: s3://redwood-benchlab/baselines/2026-02-25/inference-scaling.

Backward compatibility and rollout: new pipeline is additive — it registers new suite ids in benchmark catalog. Consumers of metrics should not be impacted. We'll run nightly for 2 weeks and monitor for changes in existing dashboards. If regressions are detected, the alert will open ENG-3420 for Triage.

Related work: linear ENG-1289 (benchmark-lab v3 rollout), ENG-3420 (auto-regressions/alerting). Links: internal runbook https://linear.redwood/ENG-1289, dashboard PR (separate) will consume these outputs.

Miguel Ortega (review): Can we make the workload configs parameterized for sequence length and batch size? Suggest templating with jinja to reduce duplication. -- m.ortega
Ethan Park (reply): Switched workload configs to jinja templates and added a small generator script (benchmark-lab/configs/gen_workloads.py). Updated tests. -- e.park
Priya Desai (approval): Verified integration smoke run on benchmark lab pool. Baseline artifacts look sane. Approving. -- p.desai
